subject.title: Remote-Only Overlay Detection Misses Some Proprietary Remote Desktop Sessions

question: Which evidence threshold and false-positive policy should govern proprietary remote desktop detection in remote-only mode?
rationale: macOS has no universal public session event, and choosing process, port, or vendor-specific signals determines whether Nameplate favors broader coverage or strict avoidance of overlays during idle clients.

options.title: Require active-session evidence
options.body: Collect connected/disconnected samples and add only signals that reliably distinguish an active viewer from an installed or idle client.

options.title: Add user overrides
options.body: Introduce explicit per-tool detection settings so users can opt into less reliable process or port heuristics.

options.title: Keep the current scope
options.body: Continue supporting virtual displays and Screen Sharing/VNC only, and document proprietary tools as best-effort or unsupported.

recommendation.title: Require active-session evidence
recommendation.body: Collect connected/disconnected samples and add only signals that reliably distinguish an active viewer from an installed or idle client.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision changes the documented behavior and false-positive tradeoff of a core visibility mode owned by the repository.
